subject: BCP Audit Response — RTO Exceptions, Key-holder Matrix, and Live Witness Window
messages:
From: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@midtownbank.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: ops-sec@midtownbank.com
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 09:15:00 -0500
Subject: Request: RTO/RPO evidence and live witness window

Hi Olga,

Thanks for taking this. Midtown's audit team is collecting artifacts for our upcoming SIG + SOC2 cross-check. Can you confirm the following for the services we discussed last week (API inference + embeddings ingestion):

- Confirm documented RTO/RPO for primary region and for cross-region failover (we need both nominal and worst-case numbers).
- Provide a KV warm-cache start trace for a warm-standby restore (we're specifically interested in the time-to-first-serving-token and any cache-populate gaps).
- A short runbook snapshot showing the exact play steps for failover, plus the current key-holder matrix for HD key custodianship.
- Can you provide a live-witness window (two-hour slot) in the next two weeks where ops can watch a controlled failover? We need date/time to coordinate stakeholders.

If you can attach any logs or runbook excerpts (redacted OK), that would speed the review. Ideally we'd like artifacts by EOD next Friday (2026-12-17).

Appreciate it — Evan
Evan Brooks
Senior InfoSec Manager, Midtown Bank
ops-sec@midtownbank.com

From: olga_petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@midtownbank.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 11:02:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Request: RTO/RPO evidence and live witness window

Hi Evan — thanks for the clear list. We're happy to provide the artifacts. Initial notes:

- Nominal RTO/RPO: Primary region (US-East): RTO 90s median for inference-tiered services under normal load; RPO < 30s for session/metadata stores. Cross-region recovery target (failover to US-West warm-standby): RTO 7–12 minutes under typical cache-warm parameters; RPO up to 60s for loose-consistency metadata.

- KV warm-cache trace: attaching a recent trace (kv-warm-cache-trace-20261205.log) showing time-to-first-serving-token when cold source is replayed into warm cache. We redacted customer identifiers.

- Runbook snapshot: attaching a redacted runbook excerpt (redacted-recovery-runbook-2026-11-30.pdf) with play steps. We will also include the key-holder matrix as an appendix.

- Live-witness: proposing the following windows: 2026-12-20 14:00–16:00 ET or 2026-12-22 09:00–11:00 ET. Each slot allows a staged failover, warm-cache verification, and post-mortem trace dump.

We're prepping the RTO/RPO matrix and an attestation PDF. Ben (cc'd) will confirm the artifact redaction guidance and whether we can provide a short video of the canary failover.

I'll aim to have the full bundle to you by 2026-12-17 EOD as requested.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Principal Security Liaison
Redwood Inference

From: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@midtownbank.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: ops-sec@midtownbank.com, procurement@midtownbank.com
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 09:34:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Request: RTO/RPO evidence and live witness window

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the early answers and the log sample. Couple of follow-ups:

1) Midtown compliance has a standing ask — under a high-throughput spike (>3x baseline) we need to understand worst-case RTO. Do you have any measured artifacts for a throttled failover scenario? If not, can you provide an exception explanation and any compensating controls?

2) For the live-witness, we need a canary-run recording or live feed for audit. If video is not possible, a synchronized log dump with trace IDs and timestamp correlation will suffice.

3) For attestation, do you have a standard signed statement (we can accept a PDF) confirming the RTO/RPO numbers and the redaction policy for shared artifacts? Procurement will need that to attach to our vendor file.

If you can map these to Deliverables (A/B/C) that helps our tracker.

Best — Evan

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: BCP Audit Response — internal artifact plan

O: quick internal note on what I recommend we provide and how to mark sensitive rows for redaction.

Deliverable A — Worst-case RTO under load: we don't have a single "3x spike" synthetic run in prod (we use rolling canaries). I can pull a stress-replay from a recent chaos exercise (2026-09-09) that simulates sustained high QPS and show RTO distribution — expect 95th pctl ~11m on that run (with cold cache). Compensating controls: priority routing to reserved pools + automatic circuit-breaker to degrade non-critical paths.

Deliverable B — Canary failover proof: we can provide a synchronized trace bundle (video optional) and the log bundle (with trace IDs). The live-witness checklist will contain the correlation plan so Midtown can tie logs to participants.

Deliverable C — Attestation: I will draft a short attestation (one page) for Olga to sign. It will state measured RTO/RPO bands, redaction rules, and the custodian contact matrix.

Attachments to include in the bundle we send to Evan: rto-rpo-matrix-2026Q4.xlsx, live-witness-checklist.pdf, kv-warm-cache-trace-20261205.log, redacted-recovery-runbook-2026-11-30.pdf.

Marissa: please confirm legal is OK with the one-page attestation language. If legal wants contract-level wording, we should route to CS/Legal.

Ben
Senior Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: olga_petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@midtownbank.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 17 Dec 2026 15:08:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Request: RTO/RPO evidence and live witness window

Evan — attaching the full bundle per the timeline. Please find:

1) rto-rpo-matrix-2026Q4.xlsx — measured med/95/99 RTOs for primary & cross-region runs; worst-case scenario row includes the chaos-exercise clip (95th pctl ~11m, cold cache).
2) kv-warm-cache-trace-20261205.log — trimmed and redacted trace showing time-to-first-serving-token and cache-populate gaps.
3) redacted-recovery-runbook-2026-11-30.pdf — play steps, role assignments, and the key-holder matrix appendix (names redacted per policy; full matrix available under NDA).
4) live-witness-checklist.pdf — runbook for the session, log correlation plan, and required Midtown attendees.
5) attestation-midtown-olga-signed.pdf — one-page signed attestation (I signed on behalf of Redwood security liaison).

Notes & answers inline to your prior questions:
- Worst-case under 3x spike: see "chaos-exercise (2026-09-09)" row in rto-rpo-matrix. We observed RTO distribution with 95th at ~11 minutes and 99th under 16 minutes for the inference API when the cache had to rebuild from a cold snapshot. Mitigations include: reserved GPU pool failover, prioritized request routing, and pre-warming scripts for KV.
- Live-witness: we can do the session on 2026-12-22 09:00–11:00 ET. We'll run a controlled failover to warm-standby, exercise cache rehydration, and stream a synchronized log dump to Midtown's ops channel. If you prefer the 12/20 slot we can still accommodate — let me know.
- Attestation: attached PDF is signed. If Procurement needs DocuSign, we can push a contract-level attestation via DocuSign link: https://docusign.com/verify/ABC-123-midtown.

If you confirm the 12/22 window I will schedule the call and send the join link + pre-session checklist.

Regards,
Olga Petrov
Principal Security Liaison
Redwood Inference
